newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - June 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - June 30.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Business leaders have been warned by the Federal Government that a goods and services tax may not be introduced unless attempts to close rorts and loopholes in the income tax system are supported. Treasurer Peter Costello and peak business bodies have disussed a trade-off of indirect tax reform for measures to broaden the direct tax base. Page 1.

After wiping out more than A$1 billion in asset values from its balance sheet, BHP Co. Ltd expects a strong profit boost over the next three years. Several rich new mining projects, and no new writedowns are expected to lift BHP's net profit to more than A$2.2 billion by 1998-99. Page 25.

The key stakeholders in Optus Communications continued a series of meetings over the weekend searching for a way for United Kingdom giant Cable & Wireless to buy out fellow foreign shareholder Bell South. Cable & Wireless is understood to be interested inlifting its stake from 24.5 per cent of Optus to beyond the foreign ownership limit, which would affect the proposed public float of Optus. Page 25.

Sydney-based engineering and project management firm CMPS&F will merge with European giant Scetauroute. Details of the merger remain confidential, but company sources say the offer values CMPS&F, which has a turnover of A$120 million, in the tens of millions. Page 27.

Two Australian Mt Kare gold exploration companies have negotiated an agreement with a local landowner company to settle a dispute over their exploration licence for Papua New Guinea. The landowner company will transfer claims it has held to Carpenter Paciic Resources NL and Ramsgate Resources NL in exchange for a 10 percent free carrying interest. Page 32.

Simeon Wines Ltd has decided to lift the cash component of its A$110 million takeover bid for Australian Vintage Wines Ltd, and seek a A$32 million share placement. AustVin directors recommended on Friday shareholders accept the Simeon bid. Page 32.
THE AUSTRALIAN

While BT Australia and Queensland Investment Corp are the main local institutional buyers of Foster's shares formerly held by BHP, the 616.6 million Foster's shares placed by BHP's brokers earlier this month have increasingly ended up in nominee companies where the beneficial owner of the stock is unknown. Page 17.

British phone company Cable & Wireless is expected to cement effective control over Optus Communications as early as today with an increase in its shareholding from 24.5 per cent to 49 per cent. Control will be taken through a A$1 billion deal acquiring Bell South's 24.5 per cent stake in the carrier. Page 17.

Close to 30 companies are believed to have applied to become full telecommunications carriers, joining Optus, Telstra and Vodafone, following deregulation of the industry tomorrow. As full carriers, new companies will be able to build their own infrastrucure, freeing them from dependence on Telstra and Optus. Page 17.

The Productivity Commission has attacked the idea of a pause in tariff cuts and has urged the Howard Government to slash tariffs for the heavily protected textile, clothing and footwear sector to 5 per cent by 2008. The proposal outlined in a draft reportto be released today challenges the Government's commitment to economic reform. Page 1.

Following a week of crisis meetings between Primary Industries Minister John Anderson and meat industry leaders, the Federal Government has imposed a full cost recovery regime on the export meat industry, which will see industry participants face large inreases in registration and inspection fees. Page 19.

Private law firms are seeking to recruit the best litigation lawyers from the Federal Attorney-General's department, ahead of the Government's move to outsourcing of its legal services in July 1988. The outsourcing will see the Attorney-General's Department operating as the Australian Government Solicitor. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

BHP managing director John Prescott says the company's A$1 billion worth of writedowns in the 12 months to 31 May will be the last for at least two years, clearing the way for it to achieve its new expanded performance criteria. BHP's profit in the year to May plunged 61 per cent to A$410 million. Page 37.

Prime Minister John Howard says workforce mobility is a factor in bringing Australia's unemployment rate closer to that of the United States. Howard said booming productivity, driven by technological advances and a flexible labour market, was largely respnsible for the United States' unemployment figures being below 5 per cent. Page 37.

On the eve of full deregulation of the telecommunications industry, Communications Minister Richard Alston has warned Optus and Telstra not to abuse their market power, encouraged consumers to demand lower prices and better services, and urged new players to look at regional markets. Page 37.

The backbench has been feted by the significant media players as it becomes apparent it will play a role in shaping any changes to media ownership rules. Lesser media players opposing the changes have put their efforts into winning over National Party memers of Parliament. Page 37.

The Oakford Property Trust has deferred the closing date for its A$25.5 million float until 14 July, because the company did not have the 500 unitholder spread required for listing on the Australian Stock Exchange. Oakford is seeking to raise the money topurchase the Oakford Quays site on Brisbane's waterfront. Page 39.

Generalised homeware and mixed apparel retailers are hoping their more buoyant May and June sales will continue to improve in the next six months. Specialised women's clothing stores, however, have been forced to offer sales and discounts. Page 39. --
THE AGE

Communications Minister Richard Alston has foreshadowed that the Federal Government may support British company Cable & Wireless' bid to take control of Optus Communications. Alston said Cable & Wireless could provide Optus with direction and has refused to rule out allowing the company to increase its stake beyond 50 per cent. Page B1.

Telstra's regulatory chief Graeme Ward has rejected the push for tariff simplification, and believes the post-deregulation period will bring even more tariffs, in the form of tailor-made packages to meet the increasingly sophisticated needs of individualcustomers. Page B1.

Communications Minister Richard Alston admits he cannot predict the future of the information revolution in terms of companies or technology, but he does not think deregulation of the telecommunications industry will produce another company like Optus, whch committed itself beyond its ability to deliver. Page B1.

Brokers and equities strategists are optimistic about the economic outlook, and believe the sharemarket will continue to rise in the next year albeit at a slower pace than the 1996-97 financial year. Commodity prices are expected to improve. Page B2.

Telstra regulatory chief Graeme Ward believes the main advantages to Telstra of the deregulation of the telecommunications industry are the lifting of the requirement to file public tariffs and the lifting of bans on price discrimination. Page B1.

Futuris Corporation is close to forming a new company from its building products division, as that part of its operations is declining and other areas are prospering. The move is expected to raise about A$250 million, with Futuris retaining in the region of 30 per cent. Page B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
